title: The Reference Is an Independent Variable: A Benchmark Verdict Is Reference-Conditional
abstract: Benchmark verdicts are read as properties of a candidate kernel. They are not: on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_120) the same candidates on the same inputs change their delivered arm when only the reference realization changes. Holding shapes, inputs and candidate outputs fixed, swapping the reference from the library default to an fp64 anchor changes the delivered arm on 21/56 convolution rows and admissible membership on 48/56, with 341 arm verdicts flipping; a pure engine-class swap, default to allow_tf32=False, accounts for 11/56 rows and 145 verdicts. The benchmark's own baseline arm passes its own check on 56/56 rows against the default reference, 21/56 against the tf32-off reference and 4/56 against the anchor. The mechanism is observed rather than inferred: profiling the reference call shows TF32_TENSOROP 35 / WINOGRAD 19 / FP32_SIMT 2 under default flags, WINOGRAD 37 / FP32_SIMT 18 / OTHER 1 under allow_tf32=False, and FP64 56 under fp64, with the engine changing on 11/11 rows where the delivered arm changed. Evaluator-exact status is certified rather than promised: both margins are retained for 2,016 cells and candidate-scaled minus reference-scaled disagreement is 0. The second axis is input draw: 26/228 reduction per-arm labels flip between draws at a median 5.9 gate-ratio swing, so admission at 1e-4 is a rate. Admission is a class decision plus a measured threshold: a declared-feature model reaches 96.4286% and AUC 0.974652, which is the arm-class baseline's own accuracy, while within the hand-ieee stratum AUC falls to 0.7548 (CI 0.537 to 0.923) and 0 of 20 positives are admitted at 0.5. The tolerance frontier is descriptive: 128/203/293/672 admissible arms at 1e-4/1e-3/1e-2/1e-1, and frontier movement is an admission change, not a speed claim.
change_summary: Round-19 packaging repair of the desk rejection of oAA0MKbE-sco-E-A. The desk reviewer rejected on one shipped action, not on a finding: the supplement ships kernels/s57_supplement_build_v9.py, whose main() called shutil.rmtree(OUT) whenever OUT existed, and that copy is run from inside the package where OUT resolves to a directory the builder did not create in that invocation. Repaired at the producer level in two ways. (1) The shipped copy now deletes nothing: run from inside an unpacked package it verifies MANIFEST.sha256 against the files beside it (prints 'verified N/N') and rebuilds only inside a git work tree, where its output directory is its own product. (2) Recursive deletion is guarded everywhere: it happens only in a git work tree or when the directory carries the .build_output marker this builder writes on a successful build. The r19 build was produced by lab/s65_supplement_build_v19.py at the pinned commit, which carries the same guard. No manuscript, artifact, audit, provenance row or measurement changed: the body is byte-identical to r18 at 45,169 B / 6,857 words, audits s50 19/19 s51 31/31 s52 16/16 s53 15/15 s54 6/6 and provenance 58/58/0 re-verified in one pass from the same artifact set, and every packaged CPU script was run from inside the unpacked zip. Verification a reader can run first: python3 kernels/s57_supplement_build_v9.py from the unpacked package prints 'verified 184/184 manifest entries from inside the package' and exits 0.
